warning_texts: Both test p values are stored as 0.0000000000 with display_digits 4; the true values are around 1e-157 (completion) and smaller (AOV), and a release should show them as below 0.0001 rather than as zero.

Part of the completion gap is pending orders, not cancellations: partner orders are about 20 per cent pending against about 14 per cent for direct in every month, and pending counts as not completed under the spec; no claim caveat tells the reader this.
The register states alpha 0.05 with bonferroni but never the adjusted per-test alpha of 0.025; the conclusions do not change because both p values are far below it.

The check plan leaves two places to auditor judgement alone: caveats_declared does not require delivered-only or net-of-refunds wording on the AOV claims, and no machine rule reads the caveat text of analysis/answers/, which is where the causal sentence sits.

recompute_estimate, recompute_test and min_group_size read clean_data/orders_clean.csv, which is not in this auditor's inputs; the auditor recomputed the same numbers from quarantine/orders.csv and they match.
Claim n is written as an integer where the metric n is a string; the values agree.
summary: All published figures in the eight claims reproduce from quarantine/orders.csv, and the claim-metric-plan chain has no mismatch. No confounding by country or month and no Simpson reversal were found. FAIL for wording: R04 says the partner channel causes lower order value through price sensitivity, which the data cannot support; both AOV claims lack delivered-only and net-of-refunds caveats; the AOV test population omits the delivered filter in the metric and claim; and the R03 and R04 hypothesis blocks leave out the registered groups.
